fixtures.source: We investigate the dual-channel AQUAL potential $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dual}}(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}x^2 - x + \ln(1+x)$ and show that its constitutive ratio $\mu(x) = x/(1+x)$ is \textbf{falsified} (2026-09-12): it leaves a constant, unscreened anomalous acceleration that exceeds the Mercury perihelion bound by $\sim10^3$, and no GW170817-safe screening removes a constant offset. The conditional uniqueness of $\mathcal{F}_{\text{dual}}$ under Pad\'e$[1/1]$ minimality, with its odds-ratio and Fisher identities, is retained as mathematics about the retired branch $\mathbf{[P]}$ and carries no physical support. The theory is rebuilt on the standard interpolation $\mu_{\text{std}}(x) = x/\sqrt{1+x^2}$, with kinetic potential $F_{\text{std}} = \tfrac12[x\sqrt{1+x^2} - \operatorname{arsinh} x]$, $F_{\text{std}}' = x\mu_{\text{std}}$. Its covariant completion is the Aether--Scalar--Tensor theory of Skordis and Z\l{}o\'snik, with free function $\mathcal{J}_{\text{std}}(\mathcal{Y}) = F_{\text{std}}(\sqrt{\mathcal{Y}})$ $\mathbf{[P]}$. In that completion $c_T = c$ holds structurally and every mode on Minkowski space propagates at or below $c$ at the published parameter points $\mathbf{[D]}$; a RAQUAL-type P(X) completion of $\mu_{\text{std}}$ would instead be superluminal along the field gradient, $c_\parallel^2 = (x^2+2)/(x^2+1)$ $\mathbf{[P]}$. In the solar system the isolated-Sun monopole tail $1-\mu_{\text{std}} \le 1/(2x^2)$ passes. The external field of the Milky Way does not: the Cassini quadrupole $Q_2$ excludes bare $\mu_{\text{std}}$ at $\approx 4.6\sigma$ at the derived $a_0$ $\mathbf{[D]}$. A phenomenological screening restores the pass without changing the SPARC fits but has no covariant realization $\mathbf{[O]}$, and AeST's stealth (exact-GR) branch recovers GR only if that branch is the one selected $\mathbf{[O]}$. Across 175 SPARC galaxies (3,391 points) we measure $a_0 = 1.161\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (95\% bootstrap interval $[0.972, 1.295]\times10^{-10}$) under $\mu_{\text{std}}$ $\mathbf{[D]}$. Horizon-temperature (KMS) matching gives $a = cH$, with the $2\pi$ cancelling $\mathbf{[P]}$, so the anchor $a_0 = cH_0/2\pi$ is a declared normalisation rather than a derivation $\mathbf{[O]}$. The pre-registered 20-galaxy $a_0(z)$ test is withdrawn: its input table could not be traced to the sources it cites $\mathbf{[X]}$. Real high-redshift kinematics (RC100 and MUSE-DARK III) place $a_0$ at $z\sim1$--$2$ at $\sim2$--$2.6$ times the local value; within that range the shape favours a constant over $H(z)$ but not significantly, and the step from $z=0$ is calibration-limited, so neither a constant nor a horizon-tied $a_0$ is excluded $\mathbf{[C]}$. The mathematics cited here, 30 Lean~4 modules, is machine-checked with no \texttt{sorry} and only the standard axioms; that certifies the mathematics, not the physical identification of each theorem. Branch selection in AeST, a covariant screening mechanism, non-linear structure formation and cluster scales remain open.
